about: Recorded, hand-written for this site (KTD11): what speech-to-text wrote and how the assistant answered, keyed by call and by what the model heard. A key is `call|parts heard` (how many parts of the caller's opening turn were finished when the turn detector fired), then the call's own detail: where the caller cut in and whether the host stopped (`stop-N`: stopped during the reply's part N; `talked-over`: no barge-in), or the read-back policy (`direct`, `confirm`). Caller turns carry the transcript; assistant turns are their clip's words (script.json), `kept` naming how many of its parts were said before the host stopped. A caller turn the host never heard is `lost`. They illustrate the sourced findings in facts.json; nothing here was measured.

status|1.note: A clean line, one question: the turn ends after Dana stops, and the order lookup answers it.
